LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN GAMES (OPTIONAL)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.6: Indigenous Kenyan Games (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indigenous Kenyan Games (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in Grade 5 CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How do indigenous counting games enhance physical fitness?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous counting game and identify the skills,

2. demonstrate different indigenous counting games while observing safety,

3. collaboratively, practise different indigenous counting games while observing safety,

4. practise different types of indigenous counting games while combining it with musical rhythm.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a virtual or live demonstration of indigenous counting game and identify the skills,
2. demonstrate different indigenous counting games while observing safety,
3. collaboratively, practise different indigenous counting games while observing safety,
4. practise different types of indigenous counting games while combining it with musical rhythm.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Games (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner takes on different roles during indigenous counting games.

• Unity: The learner works with others in indigenous counting games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Safety: The learner observes safety rules when playing indigenous counting games.

• Health and Fitness: The learner improves fitness through indigenous counting games for a healthy lifestyle.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematics: The learner uses the knowledge of counting during the performance of the indigenous counting games.
